subject: Re: On-prem / air-gapped deployment qualification - hardware & offline ops
messages:

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem / air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps

Hi Tom — great talking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call:

Recap
- Legacy Bank is evaluating a fully air-gapped, on-prem deployment of Redwood Private for transaction processing and ML enrichment.
- Primary requirements: no outbound network egress from the inference cluster, on-prem KMS/HSM integration, and a path for offline upgrades/patches.
- Timeline: procurement intent Q2; pilot target in Q3.

Immediate asks (so we can scope correctly)
1) Hardware baseline: what GPUs/servers are available or preferred (brand, model, count)?
2) Maintenance model: what are your constraints for offline upgrades (frequency, maintenance windows, approval process)?
3) Security: any additional compliance artifacts we should surface now (internal questionnaires, SCARs)?

Marcus and Vivek are on copy to answer technical and security specifics. I’m attaching a short hardware/spec checklist we usually use for air-gapped pilots. If you can fill/return, we’ll validate the sizing and give an estimated bill of materials + services.

Next step: propose a 30–45m follow-up with your infra + procurement next week to go over hardware options and procurement milestones. What time works best?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Tom Patterson <tom.patterson@legacybank.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps

Marissa / Marcus — thanks for the recap. Confirming a few points from our side:

- We do require full air-gap; cluster will sit in an isolated data center with no outbound internet.
- Preferred hardware (current estate): Dell R750xd with NVIDIA A40 GPUs (we have capacity for up to 4 nodes initially). We can explore A100 if needed but procurement lead time is longer.
- Maintenance windows are typically monthly overnight windows (Sat 02:00–06:00 local). Any major upgrades need a week lead and a formal change request.

A few questions for your team:
- How do you handle offline upgrades and kernel/OS patching for air-gapped clusters? Do you provide signed airgap bundles or do we need to build them internally?
- For KMS, we will want to use our HSM (Thales) — do you have integrations or a connector approach?

Looping infra mailbox: infra@legacybank.com — they’ll fill out the attached checklist and can push hardware specs. Procurement is targeting a decision by end of Q2 but will need a standard SOW + pricing.

Tom Patterson
Head of Infrastructure, Legacy Bank
Tom.Patterson@legacybank.com | +1 (212) 555-0987

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / air-gapped deployment qualification - next steps

Tom — thanks for the details, helpful. Short answers below and a couple of notes:

1) Offline upgrades
- We provide signed airgap bundles that include the runtime, model binaries (if customer requests model hosting on-prem), and our orchestration agent. Bundles are signed with our private key; customers can validate signatures.
- Delivery model: we support USB transfer media (we can ship encrypted USBs) or a customer-provided secure jump host where we SCP the bundle over an internally approved transfer. Installation is script-driven and can be run in the maintenance window.
- Rollback: we produce a tested rollback image and recommend a snapshot-based approach for fast rollback (we document steps in the runbook).

2) KMS/HSM
- We integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 and have prior integrations with Thales. For air-gapped deployments we support on-prem KMS with offline provisioning of keys and a manual rotation process; Vivek can outline the security controls.

3) Hardware baseline suggestion
- For an initial 4-node pilot with medium token throughput, an 8xA40 per node baseline is conservative; 4xA100 per node (if available) will give better headroom. I attached our onprem hardware spec PDF for reference.

Attachments: onprem-hardware-specs.pdf

Operational note: if you require vendor-managed patching, we offer a professional services add-on to run upgrades during your maintenance windows and provide the change documentation required by procurement.

Let me know if you want a quick technical deep-dive with our infra engineer this week.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
